split(line) splits a command line into a list of words. Whitespace outside quotes separates words. Inside single quotes every character is literal until the closing single quote. Inside double quotes a backslash followed by a double quote or by another backslash yields that one character, and any other backslash is kept as it is. def split(line):
```python
    out = []
    cur = []
    in_word = False
    i = 0
    n = len(line)
    state = None  # None, "'", '"'
    while i < n:
        ch = line[i]
        if state == "'":
            if ch == "'":
                state = None
            else:
                cur.append(ch)
            i += 1
        elif state == '"':
            if ch == '\\':
                if i + 1 < n and line[i+1] in ('"', '\\'):
                    cur.append(line[i+1])
                    i += 2
                else:
                    cur.append('\\')
                    i += 1
            elif ch == '"':
                state = None
                i += 1
            else:
                cur.append(ch)
                i += 1
        else:
            if ch == "'":
                state = "'"
                in_word = True
                i += 1
            elif ch == '"':
                state = '"'
                in_word = True
                i += 1
            elif ch == '\\':
                if i + 1 < n:
                    cur.append(line[i+1])
                    in_word = True
                    i += 2
                else:
                    cur.append('\\')
                    in_word = True
                    i += 1
            elif ch.isspace():
                if in_word:
                    out.append(''.join(cur))
                    cur = []
                    in_word = False
                i += 1
            else:
                cur.append(ch)
                in_word = True
                i += 1
    if state is not None:
        raise ValueError('unterminated quote')
    if in_word:
        out.append(''.join(cur))
    return out
```
